---
title: "Do the series wander? Panel unit roots"
---

**The question of this chapter.** Before regressing one panel variable on
another, find out whether each series returns to a stable level or wanders off
with no anchor. A wandering series has a *unit root*. Two of them can look
related when they are not, so this question comes before any estimate.

**The running example.** House prices in 49 US states over 29 years,
`HousePricesUS` [@holly2010] in **pder** [@croissant2019]. The earlier chapter
found that the states move together strongly: the CD test gives z = 53
([testing for cross-sectional dependence](panel-spat.qmd#sec-csd-tests)).
That one fact decides which tests below can be trusted.

**The map.** Each section answers one box and sends you to the next.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  Q["Do the series wander?"] --> CD{"Do units move together?<br/>CD test"}
  CD -->|"no"| G1["Tests that assume<br/>independent units"]
  CD -->|"yes"| G2["Tests that allow<br/>a common factor: CIPS"]
  G1 --> R{"Unit root rejected?"}
  G2 --> R
  R -->|"yes"| W["Which series?<br/>Hanck / Simes"]
  R -->|"no"| I1["Treat as I(1):<br/>difference, or test cointegration"]
  W --> L["Check the traps:<br/>panel shape, spatial shocks,<br/>shared trends"]
  I1 --> L
```

Every section has the same shape. **Question** in one sentence, **intuition**
in one paragraph, **the test** in words, **run it**, then **read it**: a case
where the test rejects, a case where it does not, and a case where it misleads.
A **next** box says where to go. **Recipe**, **pitfalls** and **book check**
sit in boxes at the end of each section; open them when you need them.

The math and the full literature are in
[theory note 07](theory/07-panel-unit-roots.qmd). This chapter does not need
it.

```{r}
#| label: s1-0-setup
# Shared simulators and reshapers live in R/; see R/simulate-panels.R.
devtools::load_all(quiet = TRUE)
data("HousePricesUS", package = "pder")
php <- plm::pdata.frame(HousePricesUS)
```
